bills.summary: Adds the right to basic sanitation to the Constitution's list of social rights.
Creates the statute for private security and bank security.
Sets rules for private insurance contracts and repeals parts of the Civil Code.
Places some servants, police and others in a phase-out federal staff table.
Bars ICMS on transfers of goods between establishments of the same owner.
Sets criteria and periodic evaluation for tax and financial incentives.
Includes scientific police among the public-security bodies.
Creates a credit note for micro-enterprises.
Adds a municipality to the Federal District's integrated development region.
Guarantees public hearings in budget planning.
Defines education as the vector of the country's progress.
Regulates special retirement for social-security insured workers.
Improves the Union's financial response to public calamities.
Lets cooperatives receive money from the Northeast Development Fund.
Defines who legislates on cyber-defence and cyber-security.
Uses public procurement to favour micro and small businesses.
Limits requests for review and individual injunctions in courts.
Creates the general law on environmental licensing.
Creates protection mechanisms for LGBT+ prisoners.
Allows judges from different courts to swap posts.
Changes penal-execution rules on monitoring, criminological exams and temporary leave.
Sets general rules to prevent tax disputes and favour settlement.
Sets general rights, guarantees and duties of taxpayers.
Changes how state courts elect their leadership.
Includes municipal guards and traffic agents among public-security bodies.
Creates a statute to simplify ancillary tax obligations.
Gives lottery permits extra validity.
Sets the basic organisation of the Presidency and ministries.
Includes misogyny among crimes in the anti-racism law.
Lets education funds be used for a purpose other than the one agreed.
Creates a strategy to train medical specialists within Mais Médicos.
Creates the General Sports Law.
Authorises the city of Recife to take a foreign loan with a federal guarantee.
Requires goods sold in Brazil to meet Brazil-compatible environmental standards.
Keeps municipal participation-fund coefficients for towns that lost population.
Regulates postal services provided to federal government bodies.
Creates the new fiscal framework replacing the spending cap.
Regulates recognition, demarcation and use of indigenous lands (marco temporal).
Sets tie-breaking rules at the federal tax appeals council (CARF).
Tax reform: replaces several consumption taxes with a VAT-style system.
Regulates the tax credit arising from investment subsidies.
Makes drug possession and carrying a constitutional crime mandate.
Changes the ineligibility law and election law.
Sets federal compensation to states for fuel-tax losses and related debt deductions.
Writes a time-limit (marco temporal) for indigenous land demarcation into the Constitution.
Regulates fixed-odds betting.
Extends the deadline for using Paulo Gustavo Law culture funds.
Creates a programme to cut the social-security waiting queue.
Requests a special schedule for voting on the tax reform PEC.
Sets spending for the programme that pays high-school students to stay in school.
Opens a new instalment plan for municipal pension debts.
Changes the convertible investment contract used by start-ups.
Creates the legal framework for low-carbon hydrogen with incentives.
Grants vehicle-tax (IPVA) immunity to passenger vehicles 20 years old or more.
Creates Brazil's regulated greenhouse-gas emissions trading system (SBCE).
Gives states and municipalities more time for budget transfers.
Promotes low-carbon mobility and creates sustainable aviation and green diesel programmes.
Regulates offshore wind and other offshore energy generation.
Creates compulsory insurance for road accident victims.
